new_results: For A=[[B,E],[E^T,C]] with invertible physical r-block B and Schur S=C-E^T B^{-1}E, s_j(S)>=s_{j+r}(A).
A scalar Schur peel therefore removes at most one absolute-large eigenvalue and incurs no spectral-scale loss.
If each peeled pivot has |a|>=delta ell, the normalized density recurrence T_delta(B)=2 sqrt(B/delta) has fixed point 4/delta and arbitrary depth stays below max(B_terminal,4/delta).
With partner heavy-row rho=1/(156 sqrt(2)) and threshold theta, heavy-pivot fixed point is 624 sqrt(2)/theta; the complementary bank satisfies ||b||>rho sqrt(1-theta^2) ell.

At theta=1/2 the lossless fixed point is 1248 sqrt(2)=1764.9385258416228..., improving the partner signed/shear recurrence constant by factor 4.79128784747792 when only absolute eigenvalue counts are required.
